chunks: Ibn Abī ʿUmayr and al-Bazanṭī both narrated from Jamīl, from Zurārah, from Abū Jaʿfar عليه السلام, who said:

There are two matters; whichever of them comes first for her, the divorced woman under uncertainty, who is uncertain regarding menstruation, becomes separated by it. If three white months pass over her in which there is no blood, she becomes separated by that. And if three menstrual periods pass over her, with there not being three months between the two menstrual periods, she becomes separated by menstruation.

key_terms.بَانَتْ: she became separated; her waiting period concluded
key_terms.ثَلَاثَةُ أَشْهُرٍ: three months counted in the waiting period
key_terms.ٱلْمُسْتَرَابَةُ: the woman whose condition is doubtful or uncertain

ai.seo_question: How is the waiting period determined for a divorced woman who is uncertain about her menstruation?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a legal ruling for the waiting period of a divorced woman whose menstrual state is uncertain. Her separation is determined by whichever occurs first: three bloodless months or three menstrual cycles, establishing a practical rule in divorce law.
